summary: Request: Temporary managed group + role binding for LLM debug in preprod blocked by GCP org-policy
description: Issue summary: The ML Platform team needs temporary debugger access in the preprod project (preprod-llm) to investigate a model caching regression. When we attempt to grant a short-lived group the necessary IAM role bindings, the org-level policy 'restrict-iam-bindings-to-managed-groups' blocks the change. Impact: engineers cannot impersonate the debugging service account or attach the preprod-llm-monitor role, delaying triage for an ongoing performance regression. Request: create a temporary managed group that is allowed by the org-policy allowlist (or add an explicit allowlist entry) and bind roles/iam.serviceAccountUser and roles/logging.viewer to service-account/llm-debug@preprod. Set an automatic expiry for 7 days. Background: Org policy was tightened last quarter to limit direct IAM bindings to GSuite-managed groups and SCIM-provisioned groups for auditability. The ML team cannot use the existing on-call groups because they require long-term membership and broader privileges.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Attempt in Console or gcloud to bind roles/iam.serviceAccountUser to group:llm-debuggers@external.redwood.test in project preprod-llm.
2) Console returns an error and prevents saving the policy.
3) gcloud error: gcloud iam policies set-iam-policy: PERMISSION_DENIED: Resource violates organization policy 'constraints/iam.allowedPolicyBindings'
logs:
Error detail (policy evaluation): ORG_POLICY_VIOLATION: binding 'roles/iam.serviceAccountUser' denied because principal 'group:llm-debuggers@external.redwood.test' is not in the allowed groups list for constraint 'constraints/iam.allowedPolicyBindings'.
Policy path: organizations/1234567890/policies/constraints/iam.allowedPolicyBindings
investigation_notes:
- Confirmed org policy exists at org level and lists only 'managed:' and 'scim:' group patterns.
- gcloud command used to inspect: gcloud org-policies describe constraints/iam.allowedPolicyBindings --organization=1234567890 and gcloud projects get-iam-policy preprod-llm.
- Tried adding a federated group (GSuite) but our dev GSuite provisioning for temporary groups requires admin console changes.
- Security reviewed and prefers a temporary managed group over adding individuals to a broad role.
- Options: 1) Provision a GSuite-managed group redwood-llm-debug-preprod, ask Identity team to add it to the org-policy allowlist (preferred). 2) Create a short-lived service-account proxy with narrowly scoped permissions and add individual engineers via impersonation (workaround). 3) Request an exception from OrgPolicy owners with justification and TTL.
- Recommended immediate path: create managed group + add to allowlist with a 7-day TTL. Request Identity + OrgPolicy owners to action.

resolution: Pending - plan is to: 1) Identity to create GSuite-managed group redwood-llm-debug-preprod. 2) SecOps/OrgPolicy owners to add pattern 'group:redwood-llm-debug-preprod@redwood.com' to constraints/iam.allowedPolicyBindings allowlist with a TTL entry. 3) Infra to apply the IAM bindings: roles/iam.serviceAccountUser on sa:llm-debug@preprod and roles/logging.viewer on project preprod-llm. 4) Verify audit logs and remove allowlist + group after TTL expires. If org-policy cannot be changed quickly, fallback is to create a scoped proxy service-account with short-lived keyless impersonation and document audit steps.
